description:
70 年代的滨海湾公园，有一个全新加坡都知道的地方——沙爹俱乐部。如今站在同一片空地，即使拿着老照片，也很难想象当年的热闹景象。 
这一集的来宾文史工作者李国梁，是沙爹俱乐部的“老顾客”。父亲每年生日都会带他来吃沙爹，因为祖母千叮咛万嘱咐：“孩子生日，一定要吃好的！”但当年的吃法绝对颠覆现代人的想象——吃不完的沙爹可以退回摊主再卖，吃剩的沙爹酱也会倒回锅里重复使用！ 

In the 1970s, near today’s Esplanade, there was once a famous stretch along Queen Elizabeth Walk — the legendary Satay Club. Stand there now and you’d never guess where those smoky, bustling satay stalls once stood. 
Our guest, Lee Kok Leong, remembers it vividly. Every year on his birthday, his father would bring him there because his grandmother insisted: “On a child’s birthday, he must eat something good.” 
But the old satay culture was wildly different from today — unfinished sticks could be returned and resold, and even leftover peanut sauce was poured back into the pot for the next customer!

#SG60 #新加坡60
